scope: Leakage-safe close-up shoulder curriculum for the next bounded H3 topology RSI round
summary: A ten-clip mixed-scale dataset was compiled from two rights-attributed synthetic articulated robot videos, with eight upper-body crops that make shoulder ancestry and head clearance materially more visible to training.
evidence: The immutable dataset manifest has SHA-256 14f4a55133e41dd7d79d90792a4c23545bf61ea2b998a57e40987843d5f340f0.
All 10 clips contain 39 frames at 448x256 with a 32 kHz audio stream and explicit image reference.
Two full-body clips retain global morphology context; eight upper-body clips use the declared [96, 0, 448, 256] source crop for shoulder, crossed-arm, head-clearance, and release supervision.
The train set contains two distinct articulated subjects. Same-real-scene v14 and v19 artifacts remain validation/test only and are not compiled into this train directory.
The source-crop feature rejects non-integer, negative, odd, or non-positive crop declarations and records each applied crop in the manifest.
lessons: The earlier full-body curriculum devoted too few pixels to shoulder ancestry; scale is part of supervision quality, not merely a rendering detail.
Targeted close-ups can improve the failure signal without leaking the held-out real flower scene into optimization.
Mixed-scale examples are retained to reduce the risk that close-up specialization catastrophically erases full-body appearance.
limitations: The sources are deterministic synthetic/3-D renders and remain PARTIAL task evidence rather than real-robot manipulation data.
The dataset has been compiled and visually checked but has not yet produced an accepted model checkpoint.
The close-ups emphasize visible 2-D anatomy; they do not establish physical joint dynamics.
next_actions: Use this dataset only if the completed conservative r2 round fails its frozen held-out contract.
Promote no resulting checkpoint without 124/124 topology passes plus motion-profile, task-action/EPL, scene, and temporal non-regression.
